sense: at last, after a long time

evidence: Catull. 62.2: exspectāta diū vix tandem lūmina tollit
terms.comment: “At long last” is tandem aliquandō (Cic. Cat. 1.18, 2.1) or jam tandem. In a question tandem means “pray”, “then”: quid tandem?

terms.gloss: only then, not till then, at last
terms.grammar: adverb, after a word of time: tum dēmum, nunc dēmum
evidence: Tac. Agr. 3.1: nunc dēmum redit animus

phrases.latin: dīcenda tacenda locūtus tandem dormītum dīmittitur
phrases.english: having said everything, fit to say or not, he is finally sent off to bed

phrases.latin: tertiō dēmum diē ad verticem perventum
phrases.english: it was only on the third day that they finally reached the top
so that at long last I may stop being afraid

sources: Lewis & Short: tandem · Lewis & Short: demum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 315, 337.
